stories.headline: World leaders gather for the UN General Assembly amid wars, AI concerns and deepening global divisions

sources.body: World leaders are gathering at the United Nations this week against a backdrop of wars in the Middle East and Ukraine, rising fears over artificial intelligence and mounting economic and climate pressures. The annual General Assembly will test whether the 193-member body can still bring countries together to tackle crises that increasingly transcend borders.
sources.headline: World leaders gather at UN amid wars, AI fears and global divisions

sources.body:
September 22 marks the start of the general debate, where all 193 UN member states are invited to address the General Assembly.

Here’s what to pay attention to at the UNGA

On Tuesday, nearly 130 heads of state and government are expected to begin taking the podium at the annual United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York as the high-level general debate opens.

The debate is the key event of the UNGA’s annual session, which began on September 8, when Khalilur Rahman of Bangladesh took office as president.

In this visual explainer, Al Jazeera looks at what happens at the UNGA, who will speak, and the key moments to watch.

The debate opens on Tuesday, September 22, runs through Saturday, September 26, and resumes on Monday, September 28, as no sessions are held on Sunday.

It runs in two daily sessions: from 9am to 2:45pm local time (13:00 GMT to 18:45 GMT) and from 3pm to 9pm (19:00 GMT to 01:00 GMT the next day).

Statements are expected to observe a voluntary 15-minute limit, though many run longer, and meetings continue until all scheduled speakers have spoken.

The session opens with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who introduces his annual report and is expected to give his final address, followed by UNGA President Khalilur Rahman, who formally opens the debate.

By tradition, Brazil is always the first country to speak, a practice that began in 1955 when it volunteered to open the debate, when no other country would. The United States, as the host country, usually speaks second, and President Donald Trump is expected to take the podium after Brazil on Tuesday morning, likely around 9:45am local time (13:45 GMT).

For all other member states, the speaking order is determined by the level of representation (head of state, head of government, or minister), expressed preferences, and geographic balance.

The Holy See (Vatican City), the State of Palestine, and the European Union are also invited to participate, with their speaking slots set according to their representation.

Speakers for day one are shown in the graphic below. The speaking schedule for the remaining days will be published in the coming days.

The UNGA is held at the UN headquarters, which is located along the East River in Manhattan, New York.

The complex, built between 1949 and 1952, is owned by the UN and is considered international territory. It serves as the main hub for international diplomacy.

The UNGA has not always been held in New York. The first six UNGA sessions took place in different cities, beginning in London and later including Paris. Since 1952, however, nearly all sessions have been held at the UN headquarters in New York.

Some notable exceptions include 1988, when the UNGA met in Geneva, Switzerland, after the US denied a visa to Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.

This time, for the second year running, the US has denied visas to Palestinian officials, so President Mahmoud Abbas will address the UNGA by prerecorded video after member states voted to allow it.

The Trump administration’s decision has drawn widespread criticism, with the UN asserting that it violates the Host Country Agreement, which obligates the US to allow heads of state and government to travel to New York for annual meetings and other diplomatic business, with full diplomatic immunity.
sources.headline: UN General Assembly 2026: Who is speaking and when?

sources.body:
En un contexto marcado por tensiones geopolíticas, conflictos armados y crisis mundiales , Nueva York acoge desde este martes el 81º periodo de sesiones de la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas. Será el adiós del actual secretario general, António Guterres, que se despide tras cerca de diez años al frente de una institución que vive una crisis de liquidez y de credibilidad . A la espera de ver si esta vez será una mujer quien lidere la organización y con decenas de líderes advirtiendo de una crisis del multilateralismo, la ONU busca "restaurar la confianza" e iniciar una "transformación" que le devuelva su capacidad de "generar resultados".

Guterres inaugurará el martes una Semana de Alto Nivel en la que se espera que, entre otros desafíos, se cuele en los debates el que supone la Inteligencia Artificial . Tras él, intervendrán un centenar de líderes de todo el mundo; entre ellos el brasileño Lula da Silva , seguido del estadounidense Donald Trump , que no ha cesado en subrayar la ineficacia de Naciones Unidas. Tras casi siete meses de guerra en Irán, Trump reiterará la importancia de que el país persa "no tenga un arma nuclear" ante un hemiciclo que también escuchará al presidente iraní, Masoud Pezeshkian , aunque la Administración Trump haya negado el visado a parte de su equipo.

Un año más, Washington ha negado el visado al presidente de la Autoridad Palestina, Mahmud Abás , que intervendrá por videollamada el mismo día que el primer ministro israelí, Benjamín Netanyahu . También asistirá la presidenta interina de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez , que tiene previsto reunirse con Trump mientras que su predecesor, Nicolás Maduro, continúa retenido en una cárcel federal de Nueva York, a pocos kilómetros de la ONU, tras ser capturado en enero por fuerzas estadounidenses.

En los últimos meses, distintos líderes han advertido sobre el "desmoronamiento" del orden mundial. Fue sonado el discurso del primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, en el Foro de Davos , cuando en plena escalada de tensión entre su país y Washington llamó a las potencias medianas a unirse frente a los más poderosos. El jueves, ante el Parlamento Europeo, se pronunció en la misma línea y llamó a crear "un nuevo orden justo y estable", al tiempo que advertía de que "las instituciones multilaterales en las que confiábamos se han debilitado".

"El multilateralismo e instituciones como la ONU, basadas en la cooperación y la diplomacia, no han logrado lo que se suponía que debían . Hay que examinar y reconocer sus carencias, sus debilidades y sus fracasos", expone a RTVE el profesor de la IE University Jafar Javan, con más de 30 años de experiencia en Naciones Unidas trabajando para el PNUD. Para afrontar la actual "falta de confianza en el multilateralismo" que demuestran muchos países es necesario, dice, " reconocer que el sistema tiene problemas y que, en muchos casos, ha fracasado" .

Ese orden internacional que ahora está en cuestión se inicia en la Primera Guerra Mundial, con la creación de la llamada Sociedad de Naciones, y se mantiene tras la segunda. "Se crea un sistema de seguridad en que los estados renuncian a una carrera de armamentos constante [...] y ese orden basado en normas, aunque no fueran vinculantes, restringe la capacidad de maniobra" de los Estados, explica a este medio el investigador del CIDOB y profesor emérito de Relaciones internacionales de la Universidad Autónoma de Barcelona Rafael Grasa.
sources.headline: La ONU arranca su gran cita anual y trata de recuperar su papel en un mundo en conflicto

stories.headline: Fighting in Yemen escalates as Houthis seize strategic ground and Saudi strikes hit Mokha

sources.body:
Fighting intensifies as US media say Trump called off attacks against Houthis at the last minute on Sunday.

Houthi leader Abdul Malik al-Houthi marks takeover anniversary as Yemen conflict continues

Fighting continues to rage in Yemen, with the Houthi rebels battling Saudi-backed government forces for control of strategic mountains near the Red Sea and the leader of the Iran-aligned group warning the United States against direct military involvement in the conflict.

The clashes on Monday come amid mounting regional tensions set off by the US and Israel’s war on Iran. They also followed a report by The New York Times that US President Donald Trump had ordered air attacks against the Houthis on Sunday, only to call them off at the last minute.

The renewed hostilities have killed at least 674 people and displaced more than 158,000, officials said.

According to Al Jazeera witnesses, the Houthis – who seized Yemen’s Red Sea coast this month, including the port of Mocha – are now battling to take the Kahboub Mountains in Taiz and Lahj provinces. Control of the strategic heights, which overlook the Bab al-Mandeb strait and Mayyun Island in the Red Sea, would allow the Houthis to sever the coast from the remaining government-held south.

“Since the Houthis entered Mocha and seized control of the port and later took Mayyun Island, they have been trying to advance into the mountains or make gains that would allow them to secure their rear,” said Al Jazeera’s Maha Ali, reporting from Taiz.

“Kahboub is now the main battlefield. It may remain so in the coming days given the mountain’s strategic importance and its oversight of Mayyun Island,” she said.

The fighting comes amid media reports that Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has repeatedly pressed the US to join the fight. The Houthis on Saturday claimed an attack on the Saudi capital, Riyadh, for the first time since the recent escalation.

But Washington has so far rebuffed the requests, according to reports.

The New York Times said on Monday that the Trump administration had prepared to launch air attacks on Sunday against the Houthis after new pleas from Riyadh. But it said Trump called off the attacks at the last minute, even as soldiers were loading bombs onto aircraft.

Houthi leader Abdel-Malik al-Houthi also said in an address that the US was considering a joint escalation with Saudi Arabia against his forces.

“Regional circumstances have kept the US and Israel somewhat preoccupied, creating a problem for the Saudi regime, which seeks their participation in its aggression and blockade against the Yemeni people,” the Houthi leader said. But he warned the US against escalation, saying “whoever sympathises with the oppressor … bears all consequences morally, legally, humanely.”

He also called on Pakistan and Turkiye, which have signed a mutual defence pact with Saudi Arabia, not to get involved.

Analysts said Trump’s reported reversal underscored his administration’s reluctance to take on a new military commitment in a region where US forces were already stretched thin.
sources.headline: Houthis battle for strategic heights in Yemen as thousands more flee homes

sources.body:
US president reportedly changed his mind over Saudi Arabia’s pleas for assistance as bombs were being loaded

Houthi fighters are moving to seize strategic heights in Yemen that would cut the Red Sea coast off from areas held ​by Saudi-backed forces after Donald Trump called off US strikes on the group at the last minute, reportedly as bombs were being loaded on to aircraft.

Amid increasingly heavy fighting in Yemen , which has displaced tens of thousands of people in recent weeks, the New York Times reported on Monday that the US president had flip-flopped wildly in recent days after a call from Saudi Arabia for US strikes on the Houthis.

It comes amid the Houthis’ rapid advance on the ground with the group gaining control over much of Yemen’s Red Sea coast from Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces and advancing to areas adjacent to the crucial Bab al-Mandab strait, which Saudi Arabia has used as an alternative route for oil exports bypassing disruption in the ⁠strait of Hormuz.

In the call reported by the New York Times, Saudi Arabia’s crown prince, Mohammed bin Salman, implored Trump to step in to help halt the Houthi advance after weeks of such appeals. Trump, who had been resisting joining the Saudi war in Yemen, after the call then told the Pentagon to prepare for airstrikes against the Houthis before reversing course once again, the report said.

Trump has frequently given mixed signals to Riyadh, telling reporters during a visit to Ireland earlier this month that the Houthis “called us, and they don’t want to fight us”, adding that the group was “allowing ships to pass” the Bab al-Mandab strait and that the situation would “work out very well”.

He added that the Houthi problem was limited to “one country” an apparent reference to Saudi Arabia promising to “take care of fixing that”.

The UN says hostilities in Yemen have displaced at least 125,000 people since the start of September. Taiz city has received the largest number of displaced persons, taking in up to 86,000 Yemenis since the recent escalation began.

The rapid advance by the Iran-aligned group this ‌month has extended the wider Middle East conflict to a new theatre and further threatened global energy supplies.

Washington has so far rebuffed repeated pleas from Prince Mohammed to join the fight in Yemen with the Houthis claiming on Saturday they had fired on Riyadh, where columns of smoke were visible near the main airport.

The Yemeni president, ⁠Rashad al-Alimi, ⁠spoke to Trump on Sunday, requesting ‌support for his ‌UN-recognised government in its fight against the Houthis. Trump ⁠made no direct pledge ​of military ​support during ​the call, sources said.

Saudi Arabia has launched hundreds of strikes in recent days on Houthi positions in the strategic Kahboub mountains, according to the group, but making little impact on the ​advance of its fighters.

Fighting has centred on the outskirts of the remote Al-Wazi’iyah district in Taiz province and Ras al-Ara along the Indian Ocean coast, which separate the Red Sea coast from the city of Aden, where the government is based. The Houthis aim to secure the rear of their forces around the Bab al-Mandab strait by taking control of the mountains, which would also allow them to open new ‌fronts, according to ⁠sources who spoke to Reuters.
sources.headline: Houthis move to seize strategic terrain after Trump calls off airstrikes at last minute

stories.headline: Typhoon Dujuan kills at least four in Japan as evacuations are ordered for millions

sources.body:
Four people have died in Japan after Typhoon Dujuan battered Tokyo and surrounding prefectures with torrential rains and destructive winds, local reports said.

The storm cut power for 50,000 people and caused the suspension of hundreds of flights. Most evacuation orders were lifted on Tueday as the storm pulled away from Japan's eastern coast.

At the height of the storm on Monday, authorities warned of an "imminent threat to life" and urged 1.9 million people to move to shelters.

The fatalities were from landslides in Kanagawa and Chiba prefectures. Six others were reported missing, public broadcaster NHK reported.

Dujuan had sustained winds of 130km/h (81mph) and gusts of 194km/h.

The typhoon is the latest in a series of storms in the Pacific, made more intense by the "super El Niño", which has warmed the ocean, fuelling the formation of storms.

Authorities had advised the public to pay attention to weather information.

Dujuan, which is Japan's 25th typhoon of the year, hit in the midst of a five-day holiday and forced the cancellation of several events.

Concerts scheduled for Monday at the Rock in Japan music festival were cancelled, while the Tokyo Game Show, a video game convention, also cancelled Monday's programme.

Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi offered her condolences in a post on X to those who lost their lives in the typhoon, before saying she would be continuing with her scheduled trip the United States as planned.

"With a sense of urgency, I instructed Chief Cabinet Secretary Takehara and Minister Hosono to respond with utmost preparedness," she wrote, before saying she had boarded a flight to the US.

She will be speaking at the UN General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, and will meet with US President Donald Trump.

The Yokosuka City Fire Department told the BBC that a woman in Kanagawa prefecture, aged in her 60s, was believed to have been buried alive after a landslide swept the house she lived in.

Following a search by rescue crews, she was found inside the home and pronounced dead, NHK reported.

Separately, Sodegaura City Fire Department in Chiba prefecture told the BBC a man in his 50s was rescued after getting trapped while working to clear debris at a landslide site.

The department said the worker fell into a bamboo thicket, along with some heavy machinery. He was then taken to hospital before his death was confirmed, according to local reports. Police are investigating the details of the incident.

Some research suggests that Japan has become more exposed to destructive storms, but climate change is not thought to be increasing the number of these storms globally, and could even make them less common in some regions.

As temperatures rise, typhoons that do form are likely to become more intense on average, however.

Warmer ocean waters mean storms can pick up more energy, leading to higher wind speeds.

And because a warmer atmosphere can hold more moisture, these storms could also bring heavier rainfall.

This year, El Niño - the natural weather phenomenon bringing warmer water to parts of the tropical Pacific - is another factor.
sources.headline: Four dead after powerful Typhoon Dujuan lashes Japan

sources.body:
Rescuers search for missing in collapsed homes after storm causes landslides, travel chaos and power outages

Typhoon Dujuan has killed at least four people and injured 22 in Japan , while tens of thousands of houses near Tokyo remained without power after the storm swept through the region, authorities said on Tuesday.

Dujuan – which brought violent winds of 144km/h (89mph) – was moving away from Japan on Tuesday morning, allowing authorities to downgrade most heavy rain and landslide warnings.

But the typhoon had already caused deaths, destruction and widespread chaos, including disruption of some events at the Asian Games and forcing the early closure in Tokyo of the one of the world’s biggest video game trade fairs.

The city of Yokosuka in Kanagawa prefecture, near Tokyo, reported multiple landslides because of the torrential rain. Mud flowing into a home killed a woman in her 60s in Yokosuka, the public ​broadcaster NHK said. Police and firefighters said they were trying to find a couple in their 70s.

Local authorities in Chiba, near Tokyo, said three people were killed in a series of landslides that hit the prefecture, according to NHK. Two people, believed to have been inside homes that collapsed, were missing.

Officials said 45,000 households ​were still ​without electricity in Chiba on Tuesday morning.

The storm forced Japan Airlines to cancel 135 flights and All Nippon Airways to scrap 140, and more than 1.6 million residents in and around Tokyo were urged to evacuate on Monday, according to the Fire and Disaster Management Agency. The evacuations were not mandatory.

Although Dujuan weakened as it moved north-east, it dumped record rainfall in parts of the Tokyo area.

Oshima, an island about 120km south of central Tokyo, was drenched with 832mm of rain over 48 hours, more than double its average rainfall for the whole of September, NHK reported. And rainfall in Tokyo’s Edogawa ward reached a record 282.5mm over 24 hours.

Japan often sees strong typhoons in the late summer and early autumn. But scientists say human-driven climate change is intensifying the risk posed by heavy rains because a warmer atmosphere holds more water.

Typhoon Dujuan is the latest extreme weather event in a ⁠year of unusually intense rain, floods and tropical ​cyclones that have hit ‌regions across ‌the globe, from east Asia to North America ‌and Europe.
sources.headline: At least four people killed in Japan as typhoon Dujuan triggers heavy rain, landslides

stories.headline: Russian strikes kill three in Ukraine as Zelenskyy arrives in the US for the UN summit

sources.body:
Overnight missile and drone attacks hit several Ukrainian regions as world leaders gather in New York for the UN General Assembly.

Russian forces have launched widespread attacks targeting industrial sites and critical energy infrastructure across several regions of Ukraine, killing at least three people and knocking out power to nearly 100,000 residents, Ukrainian officials said.

The strikes overnight hit industrial facilities simultaneously in the Dnipropetrovsk region, including Dnipro, Pavlohrad and Kryvyi Rih, the hometown of President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, regional Governor Oleksandr Hanzha said on Telegram on Tuesday.

Three people were killed and six others were wounded in Dnipro, where missiles, drones and artillery heavily damaged business and warehouse premises, Hanzha said.

Ukraine’s air force said Moscow’s overnight barrage involved 212 drones, four cruise missiles, and an unspecified number of Oniks antiship and ballistic missiles.

The strikes also damaged energy infrastructure. An attack on a power facility left nearly 100,000 consumers without electricity in the northern region of Chernihiv, while in the Poltava region, Governor Vitalii Diakivnych said a “massive” Russian attack hit an industrial enterprise and a critical infrastructure facility.

The Russian Ministry of Defence confirmed its forces carried out major strikes, stating it hit industrial and military facilities, the fuel and energy sector, port infrastructure and sea vessels operating for the Ukrainian military.

Meanwhile, Ukrainian drones targeted Russia’s Samara region along the Volga River, killing one person and injuring four, according to the local governor. The region hosts critically important facilities, including oil refineries.

The Russian Defence Ministry said its air defence units intercepted and destroyed 297 Ukrainian drones across various regions overnight.

The attacks come as Zelenskyy arrived in New York for the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) , where talks on ending the war are set to be high on the agenda as nearly 130 heads of state gather.

The Ukrainian president wrote on X that a “drone deal” was ready to be signed to bolster air defence and secure funding for the war effort.

“Of course, Ukraine’s number one priority is bringing peace closer and protecting the lives of our people,” Zelenskyy posted. “There are concrete security proposals and de-escalation measures that could bring the end of the war closer. We are working to strengthen air defence and ensure sufficient financing for Ukraine.”

He said, “Around 20 meetings are planned, including with the US president, European leaders, US senators and members of the House of Representatives, heads of international organisations, leading American companies and think tanks.”

Zelenskyy met French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday and is likely to meet US President Donald Trump on Tuesday.

Earlier, Macron also met Trump, after which he said the two countries agreed to work together to secure a moratorium on strikes targeting energy networks and civilian infrastructure in Ukraine. Both Zelenskyy and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov are set to address the UNGA later this week.
sources.headline: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill three as Zelenskyy arrives for UN summit

stories.headline: Major US media outlets boycott Trump events after the White House bans several news organizations

sources.body:
Major US television networks suspended their pooled coverage of President Donald Trump on Monday in response to CNN, Politico and MS NOW being barred from the White House.

Trump announced the ban on Friday as he accused the organisations of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration. The companies said their reporters were denied access to the building on Saturday.

The three US outlets have since said they will sue the Trump administration in a bid to "defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports".

Shortly after, the White House launched its own streaming channel, Trump TV, which operates a 24/7 feed of clips of the president.

Several other US outlets have also announced that they would not participate in coverage of pooled events, with some, including the New York Times and Washington Post, saying they would not share still images from Trump events on Monday.

It meant there was no network TV footage of Trump boarding Air Force One or arriving in New York to attend the UN general assembly.

Trump also took part in a ribbon-cutting ceremony for the new Marine One helipad on the White House South Lawn. The event was streamed on the White House site but his comments were inaudible.

The president did later appear on television following a meeting with the Mayor of New York Zohran Mamdani. He told the president that all members of the media would be welcome at the press conference.

Trump said: "It's interesting because, they said they were going to boycott me, but they never boycott me, so I wasn't very worried about that. Look at all that press."

The pool involves media organisations sharing material to save on costs and space when broadcasting presidential events to the American public.

Fox News Washington bureau chief Bryan Boughton, who currently holds a rotating role helping to organise media TV crews covering the White House, wrote in an email seen by the BBC that "effective today, the TV pool will not be covering designated as pool coverage" of Trump.

The message said the move followed the White House "preventing" CNN from fulfilling its pool duties for Trump's trip to New York and that "there will be no replacement pool put in place".

The three media organisations banned from the White House filed a lawsuit on Monday in US District Court in Washington.

A joint statement announcing the legal action said: "Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting.

"Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference."
sources.headline: Major US outlets boycott shared Trump coverage in protest at media ban

stories.headline: British Columbia sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over the Tumbler Ridge school shooting

sources.body:
Canadian province alleges deadly attack could have been prevented if company had warned police of shooter’s ChatGPT use

British Columbia has sued OpenAI in California , saying a mass shooting at a school in the province could have been prevented if the company had warned local ⁠law enforcement that the shooter ⁠had used ChatGPT to ​plan the massacre.

The lawsuit filed in San Francisco federal court on Monday names OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, as defendants. It is seeking damages to fund recovery efforts in the province after the February attack, as well as an order directing changes to the way the company handles ChatGPT conversations that could lead to violence.

Nine people, primarily children, were killed in the school shooting in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia. The shooter, Jesse Van ⁠Rootselaar, had been flagged by the company’s safety team after her conversations about gun violence, but the company did not alert police.

Altman published a letter ​to the community saying he was “deeply sorry” OpenAI had not contacted ‌law enforcement. He promised reforms, but never ‌followed through, despite efforts from British Columbia’s attorney general to engage, the lawsuit says.

The school where the shooting took place is in the process of being ‌demolished , and the province has been forced to absorb the costs of a replacement school, mental health care and other effects of the shooting, according to the lawsuit.

A spokesperson for OpenAI , Drew Pusateri, called the Tumbler Ridge shooting an unspeakable tragedy. “OpenAI remains committed to working collaboratively with government and law enforcement officials, and continuing to advance our ongoing safety work.”

British Columbia’s lawsuit comes after more than 30 family members of victims and others affected by the attack filed lawsuits in California, accusing the company of opting out of a chance to prevent ‌the shooting.

Van Rootselaar shot her mother and stepbrother at home before killing an educational assistant and five students aged 12 and 13 at her former school on 10 February, according to police. Van Rootselaar, who was 18, then died by ​suicide.

Van Rootselaar’s interactions with ChatGPT were first flagged by the company in June 2025. Safety team members recommended contacting police, but Altman and other OpenAI leadership overruled them, the lawsuit says, citing OpenAI whistleblowers who spoke to the Wall Street Journal in the wake of the shooting.

The shooter’s account was deactivated, but she was able to get a new account and continue using the platform to plan her attack.

After publication of the Wall Street Journal article, the company said the ⁠account was flagged by systems that identify “misuses of our models in furtherance of violent activities”, but the issues did ​not meet its internal criteria for reporting to law ​enforcement.

The lawsuit comes after a series of ​cases against OpenAI have been filed in US state and federal courts in recent months over claims ChatGPT facilitated violence, ​including lawsuits related to a mass ‌shooting at Florida State ​University last year.
sources.headline: British Columbia sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over Tumbler Ridge mass school shooting

sources.body:
A Canadian province is suing OpenAI over its alleged failure to notify authorities about concerning user interactions on ChatGPT prior to the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting.

The company has previously apologised for not flagging Jessie Van Rootselaar's account to law enforcement before the 18-year-old killed eight people, including six children, in February.

British Columbia attorney general Niki Sharma said the lawsuit, filed to a US federal court on Monday, raised questions about "the responsibilities of technology companies when they become aware of credible threats of serious violence".

Families of those killed or injured in the shooting have filed separate lawsuits against OpenAI.

Media reports revealed that Van Rootselaar's ChatGPT activity was flagged by OpenAI's safety team for references to gun violence months before the attack, but the company did not alert local authorities.

In April, OpenAI's chief executive Sam Altman apologised to the families of the victims.

"I am deeply sorry that we did not alert law enforcement," Altman wrote in an open letter.

The BBC has requested comment from OpenAI regarding the latest lawsuit.

"To date, OpenAI has not taken meaningful steps to address the concerns raised by survivors, families and the Tumbler Ridge community," Sharma said in a statement.

"The company still has an opportunity to demonstrate accountability by strengthening safeguards, improving transparency and taking concrete action to help prevent similar tragedies in the future."

Speaking to reporters on Monday, Sharma said she had not read the contents of the OpenAI chats.

"We have asked OpenAI to disclose these chats. They have refused. We should all be asking them: Why?" she said, according to CBC .

Sharma said the lawsuit was filed in California, as the alleged decision not to report the shooter's ChatGPT account occurred in that US state, according to AFP.

Sharma told reporters that any financial damages won by the province would go towards rebuilding the secondary school.
sources.headline: Canadian province sues OpenAI over Tumbler Ridge school shooting

stories.headline: Republicans expand their midterm defense as economic and tariff concerns put deep-red seats at risk

sources.body: Republicans are playing defense deep in their own territory as voter anger over price hikes puts more House and Senate seats in play in the midterms. New rounds of big spending, visits from Trump administration officials and private conversations among top GOP officials overseeing the battle for control of Congress reveal a party rushing to shore up red seats and states President Donald Trump won handily in 2024. In the House, the fight has expanded far outside the few-dozen seats considered the most competitive as Republicans start to unleash their massive warchest: Since Aug. 1, more than $110 million in ad bookings have gone toward Republican-held districts so red that Trump won them by double digits. In the Senate, Republicans are racing to shore up Ohio GOP Sen. Jon Husted as the Midwest struggles under the weight of Trump's tariffs and high diesel prices. Trump and Vice President JD Vance are both expected to travel to the state before the midterms to boost Husted, according to four people familiar with the matter who were granted anonymity to discuss not-yet-public plans. GOP leaders are also trying to keep a handle on contests in Iowa and Kansas — and they've quietly begun deprioritizing Georgia and even North Carolina, which a growing number of Republicans are privately bracing for Democrats to flip. “We need to stop the contagion,” said one senior GOP official, who, like others, was granted anonymity to speak candidly about the midterm landscape.   “The map is hilariously big right now,” said one national Republican pollster. Since Aug. 1, nearly two-thirds of advertising funds in House races have been booked or spent in races with GOP incumbents, according to a POLITICO analysis of data from AdImpact, which tracks political advertising. That includes nearly $18 million to embattled Rep. Max Miller in Ohio’s 7th District; $14.6 million to Texas’ 15th District where Monica De La Cruz faces a challenge from Tejano Singer Bobby Pulido; $9.6 million in Alaska where Rep. Nick Begich faces a challenge from independent Bill Hill; and millions more to other districts that Trump carried by double digits two years ago. The GOP holds a massive cash advantage over Democrats — which, for now, means they can afford to spend more broadly. Republican groups are dividing up the spending deluge in the final weeks ahead of the midterms, with Trump’s MAGA Inc. affiliated super PAC spending heavily to shore up safer red seats and deter Democrats from pushing into those races. “The voter enthusiasm [for Republican voters] is not where it needs to be but that’s where a money advantage can make a really big impact,” said Mark Bednar, a GOP strategist and former communications director for then-Speaker Kevin McCarthy. Republicans have adjusted their Senate map expectations: They’re still bullish about Maine, Michigan and New Hampshire. They’re not as optimistic about North Carolina — which Trump won in 2024 — but they are hoping to force Democrats to spend more there. Republicans are more concerned about Alaska and Texas. And their worries about Ohio have escalated amid soaring diesel prices and backlash to tariffs — challenges they’re also confronting in Texas, Iowa, Michigan and Kansas .  Already two battleground candidates have called for ends to the Iran war, pointing to the high prices: Iowa GOP Senate nominee Ashley Hinson , whose team has grown increasingly wary of the tight race and Michigan GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers . Both Hinson and Rogers use top Trump pollster Tony Fabrizio to guide their campaigns. The White House did not respond to a request for comment on Hinson’s and Rogers’ remarks. Senior GOP operatives' own internal polling shows Trump's approval underwater in deep red states across the country. And an Iowa poll conducted last week by a Democratic-leaning pollster found Democrat Josh Turek with a one-point lead in the Senate race and Trump’s approval at 43 percent in the state he won by more than 13 percentage points in 2024, according to a copy of the poll obtained by POLITICO. “As more races come online, it very clearly is a defensive map for Republicans across the country,” said a national GOP strategist working on multiple battleground races. In Ohio, Republicans are optimistic that their attacks on former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown’s voting record are starting to break through, based on recent internal polling. But they’ve been conveying to outside groups for weeks that they need help reinforcing vulnerable incumbents like Husted. On Monday, the pro-crypto super PAC Fairshake said it planned to unleash $30 million against Brown, who was the top Democrat on the Banking Committee before losing reelection in 2024 — fueled in part by more than $40 million against him from Fairshake that year. “The stakes go far beyond one Senate seat,” Amy Natoce, a Husted campaign spokesperson, said in a statement. “Control of the Senate will determine which agenda moves forward in Washington: Sherrod Brown's out-of-touch socialist agenda, or Jon Husted’s agenda of lower taxes, a secure border, and an economy that rewards hard work.”   One Michigan Republican acknowledged the immense weight of the tariffs in races across the battleground state — including in the marquee Senate contest between Rogers and progressive Abdul El-Sayed, as well as across competitive House races. "Everywhere we go, we are getting hammered on it,” the Michigan Republican said. "It's crushing us." Even skeptical Republicans have been quietly checking in with their colleagues to see if the panic in redder territory is borne out in reality on the ground or just overblown polling. One GOP lawmaker who spoke to Hinson and her campaign team was somewhat surprised by their answers. “It’s real,” that House Republican told POLITICO. And POLITICO overheard a senior member of Kansas’ Republican party leadership complaining about their state’s tighter-than-expected race at the GOP’s midterm convention in Dallas earlier this month. GOP Sen. Roger Marshall, the person said, was in some trouble even as Republicans tried to dismiss the seriousness of his Democratic challenger, Adam Hamilton. Trump and Vance, meanwhile, continue to travel to states they won by double digits in 2024 to stump for Republican candidates, as Trump-aligned super PACs hammer the airwaves in far more red territory than blue. Recently-formed super PACs aligned with MAGA Inc. — Trump’s main spending vehicle that holds more than $400 million — have spent in 42 House districts so far, 30 defensive and 12 offensive. On average, they are spending in areas that voted for Trump by 7.9 points in 2024, according to a POLITICO analysis. The PACs are even spending in some districts Trump carried by 15 points as a way to shore up Republicans and deter Democratic advances, according to Republicans involved in the conversations. Major Republican super PACs, including the Trump aligned-super PACs and party-linked groups, have spent in more than two dozen GOP-held seats where Trump won by at least 5 points in 2024. “Republicans aren’t taking anything for granted this cycle and will deploy whatever resources necessary to protect our majorities and prevent Democrats from taking control,” RNC spokesperson Natalie Baldassarre said in a statement. The NRSC argued that “Democrats lack quality candidates and a clear path to victory,” so the party is “feigning optimism” and looking to candidates who have lost before, including Brown, “to somehow deliver [a] majority.” The NRCC said their opposition is “too broke to fight back.” The geography of the Senate map still favors the GOP this cycle: Democrats have to defend all of their seats, while flipping four Republican-held ones, to take control of the upper chamber. Republicans believe they have a real shot at flipping New Hampshire , and public polling shows Minnesota’s Senate race closer than expected, forcing Democrats to pay some minor attention to a state Kamala Harris won in 2024. And Republicans are still hopeful that their mid-decade gerrymandering push could still give them a structural advantage as they fight to defend the House. Republicans won the redistricting war that erupted last summer and will likely net at least six seats from it. But as economic concerns continue to dominate — with little relief in sight — Democrats are growing increasingly bullish. “You know, I look at places like Kansas where I never thought we’d have a chance, or South Carolina or even Mississippi, these places are longshots, but they look like they’re competitive,” Sen. John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.) said. For their part, senior Republicans have been working the problem from two ends, trying to gently persuade Trump in private conversations to back off some of his recent policy moves and wind down the war in Iran — while also organizing a wave of cash reinforcements across the growing map to try to stem the bleeding. GOP lawmakers pressed Trump officials at their Dallas convention and since then to take emergency actions around fuel prices and refinery capacity. A band of House Republicans led an unsuccessful attempt to vote on a federal gas tax suspension until after Election Day. And, over the weekend, Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) posted several direct appeals to Trump, asking why he hasn’t put an embargo on diesel exports. But many are convinced the bleeding won’t stop until voters get some relief at the pump. “The question is: How much longer can we go?” one senior House Republican said.
sources.headline: ‘We need to stop the contagion’: GOP ramps up midterms defense in Trump states

sources.headline: Flights halted at several major airports in Northeast due to tech problems

sources.body:
Hundreds of flights have been delayed at major airports in the US after construction workers accidentally cut a cable needed for air traffic control.

Ground stops and delays were issued on Monday afternoon for airports in New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Massachusetts.

Hours later, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the cable had been repaired and airports would resume normal operations, though delays were still expected.

The major east coast disruption came ahead of the UN General Assembly (UNGA) in New York City on Tuesday, which is expected to be attended by scores of world leaders arriving into New York-area airports.

That includes UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who managed to board his flight before the delays began and arrived as planned.

The delays happened after the damaged cable impacted the Terminal Radar Approach Control system, which is used to guide planes during takeoff and landing, transport officials said.

New Jersey public transportation agency NJ Transit told CBS News, the BBC's US partner, that its construction workers had accidentally severed the line and that markers had been wrongly placed at the digging site.

The BBC has reached out to NJ Transit for comment.

Duffy earlier said the damage was caused by workers from Amtrak, the US national operator of intercity railroad service, who were doing the construction work. This "caused a telecom outage" which forced the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to ground flights, Duffy posted on X.

An Amtrak spokesperson said in a statement, reported by US media, that the incident involved a NJ Transit contractor. Telecommunications company Verizon, which owns the cable, also said it was not responsible.

The severed cable was actually a backup network, and the error was only discovered after the primary circuit failed, according to the head of the FAA, Bryan Bedford.

Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey - one of the three major airports that services New York City - was the most heavily impacted by today's air traffic control disruptions, according to flight-tracking website FlightAware.

It reported that 267 departing flights were delayed today, while a further 257 flights destined for Newark were also delayed.

John F Kennedy International Airport and LaGuardia Airport, both in New York, were also affected, as was Philadelphia International Airport.

One passenger, Douglas Tewnion, said he boarded a flight to New York from Edinburgh and that his plane had been diverted to Boston, Massachusetts instead.

He told the BBC that, two hours after his flight was due into New York, he and the other passengers were still "sitting on the same plane, on the tarmac at Boston with no information".

Though "everyone is in good spirits", Tewnion said "it's just a pain" to see two more hours waiting added onto a lengthy flight.
sources.headline: Flights at major US airports delayed after cable cut by construction workers

stories.headline: New York Governor Kathy Hochul considers further AI safeguards, including a possible kill-switch requirement

sources.body: ALL EYES ON GRACIE: Mayor Zohran Mamdani is expected to sit down with President Donald Trump at Gracie Mansion this afternoon, their third in-person meeting in less than a year and the latest wrinkle in one of the strangest relationships in American politics. Since Mamdani’s first, shockingly cordial meeting with Trump at the White House last November, political observers have scratched their heads about the democratic socialist mayor playing nice with the Republican president despite their deep disagreements on … just about everything. Ostensibly, Mamdani is putting his personal distaste for Trump aside and betting it’s best for New York City to keep things cordial so as to avoid drawing the president’s ire. But as resistance to Trump remains animating for Democrats nationally ahead of November’s midterms, Mamdani’s strategy for engaging with him stands out. Earlier today, Gov. Kathy Hochul made clear that she, for one, has no plans to meet with Trump while he’s in New York. “I speak to him on the phone whenever I need to,” she told reporters in Manhattan. Hochul, who’s facing reelection in November and tends to directly criticize Trump more frequently than Mamdani, said it was her understanding that the mayor agreed to host the president at Gracie Mansion during a previous conversation at the White House. “The mayor and [Trump] said that when he's back in town again, he would go to Gracie Mansion,” the governor said. “I don't have a Gracie Mansion to invite him to.” Still, Hochul said there’s an opportunity for Mamdani to use the Gracie confab to push Trump on releasing federal funding for New York, including for law enforcement , that she said the president’s administration has been withholding. “We have to continue fighting for what New York needs,” she said. Mamdani’s office wouldn’t say who requested today’s meeting or share specifics about the expected focus in advance, only saying the mayor will talk to Trump about “issues affecting New York City.” A Mamdani spokesperson said the mayor will elaborate on what was discussed at a post-meeting press conference that Trump isn’t expected to attend. After the appointment at Gracie, Trump is slated to meet with French President Emmanuel Macron before headlining a couple Republican fundraisers. By contrast, after his Trump tête-à-tête, Mamdani will have dinner with Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders, who’s in the city to headline a United Nations Charter event this evening that will also feature pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil, a person familiar with the plans who was granted anonymity to discuss them told Playbook. The Queens-born Trump is in town ahead of his Tuesday address to the United Nations General Assembly. Maintaining a relationship with Trump isn’t without risk for Mamdani. As Trump remains deeply unpopular amid the war in Iran and other controversies, some Democrats are privately questioning why the mayor sees a need to keep interacting with the president. But so far, Mamdani hasn’t faced any significant pushback from his hard-left base over his engagements with Trump, with leaders of the local chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America largely viewing it as the mayor acting in the city’s best interests. — Chris Sommerfeldt and Madison Fernandez  From the Capitol EYES ON AI: Hochul floated requiring safeguards like an artificial intelligence “kill switch” as part of state-level interventions to address the rapidly evolving technology. During a Monday event in Manhattan rolling out next steps for enacting the RAISE Act, New York’s landmark AI safety law that is set to go into effect in January, the governor said she’ll “look closely at additional ways to build on” the legislation — including AI kill switches “if they're deemed feasible and in the best interest of our state.” The governor in recent days has vowed to take additional AI-related actions beyond the RAISE Act, but has not specified what that might look like. Her suggestion of a kill switch comes days after California Gov. Gavin Newsom issued an executive order to explore such a requirement for AI companies’ most-advanced models. Some in the tech industry have argued implementing one is not technically feasible. Federal legislation to enact a kill switch requirement is currently stalled in Congress. When asked to expand on the prospect of requiring a kill switch, Hochul said that “all options are on the table,” but wasn’t making a commitment. “We're going to do the research and make the decisions that are thoughtful to protect New Yorkers,” she said. “We'll go as far as we need to to protect people of this state and ultimately this country in the absence of other leadership.” Read more from Madison Fernandez in POLITICO Pro . MORE BLAKEMAN MONEY: Billionaire former casino developer Steve Wynn has donated $1 million to the main super PAC supporting Republican Bruce Blakeman’s gubernatorial bid, records filed with the state Board of Elections this morning show. The committee, Strong and Safe New York, has now raised $5.3 million since July. Wynn has been a top donor to national Republican causes for over a decade. His most recent large donations in New York came last year, when he gave $361,000 to the state GOP and $500,000 to a super PAC boosting Andrew Cuomo’s mayoral bid. — Bill Mahoney FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL ENDORSEMENT CORNER: Rep. Jared Golden (D-Maine) endorsed GOP Rep. Mike Lawler in his reelection campaign in suburban New York, Golden wrote in an opinion article published Monday. Lawler is facing a tough reelection campaign against Democrat Cait Conley in one of the biggest House battlegrounds this November. The lawmakers have previously collaborated to advance the Northeast Lobsterman Protection Act, and are both members of the centrist Problem Solvers Caucus. Golden, who is not running for reelection, was one of two House Democrats to break with the party and twice vote in favor of the Republican legislative agenda earlier in September. “Mike Lawler has been a true partner to me and a friend to fishing families he will never represent,” Golden wrote. “I strongly back him, and I hope voters send him back to work. Wherever you live, find the members who pass laws with the other party, and keep them.” House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called the cross-aisle endorsement a “smoke and mirrors ploy” that “will do nothing to change the outcome of the race.” “In desperation, [Lawler] is peddling an 11th hour endorsement from a retiring Congressmember who represents an out of town district more than 400 miles away,” Jeffries said in a statement. “Mike Lawler is an unadulterated phony who has never shown bipartisan courage when it matters.” Read more from POLITICO’s Elleiana Green . ON THE AIRWAVES: With fewer than 50 days to go before Election Day, House Democrats’ main super PAC is making its first TV ad buy in support of Conley on Monday. The House Majority PAC said it is reserving $1.2 million on cable in the Hudson Valley contest. (An additional $1.2 million is going toward fighting Republican Rep. Tom Kean Jr.’s re-election in New Jersey, which is also covered by the New York City media market.) HMP said earlier this year that it didn’t include the high-dollar NYC media market in its initial reservations because it was “prioritiz[ing] markets where rates increase significantly.” Republicans have been largely outpacing Democrats in NY-17 on the ad spending front, thanks to significant buys from super PACs backed by the president and House leadership. From the beginning of September through Election Day, the GOP has placed $15 million on ads across broadcast, cable, CTV and digital platforms, according to ad tracker AdImpact. The new HMP spend is the biggest from an outside Democratic group so far, but still leaves a large gap between the parties. Democrats have placed around $3 million on advertising in the period between September and Election Day, with the largest chunk coming from the Conley campaign. — Madison Fernandez IN OTHER NEWS IN OTHER NEWS: — JUDGES CASH IN: Brooklyn Democratic Party leaders have raked in $190,000 in contributions from judges and judicial candidates since 2012, raising some ethical and legal concerns. ( New York Post ) — AFFORDABILITY AHEAD: Anthony Shorris, the mayor’s new pick for the president of the New York City Economic Development Corporation, laid out a vision for solving the city’s affordability crisis that goes beyond Mamdani’s vision for five city-owned grocery stores. ( The New York Times ) — BUY NOW, PAY LATER: The Mamdani administration is pushing Albany for tougher ‘buy now, pay later’ regulation, as many New Yorkers use the plans to pay for basic essentials, sinking deeper into debt. ( amNY ) Missed this morning’s New York Playbook? We forgive you. Read it here .

stories.headline: Judge sends Begoña Gómez, the Spanish prime minister's wife, to trial by jury over alleged influence peddling and embezzlement

sources.body:
Justo en el día que volvía de vacaciones y a menos de una semana de jubilarse, el juez Juan Carlos Peinado envió este lunes a juicio oral con jurado popular a Begoña Gómez , mujer del presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, por los presuntos delitos de tráfico de influencias y malversación, y a su exasesora en la Moncloa, Cristina Álvarez, por este último.

Peinado pone así fin a una investigación que arrancó hace casi dos años y medio a raíz de una denuncia del sindicato Manos Limpias y ahora será la Audiencia Provincial de Madrid la que fije la fecha de juicio, algo que se podría prolongar entre cuatro y ocho meses.

Durante todo este tiempo, el magistrado ha achacado y dejado de achacar a Gómez diferentes delitos, ha citado a declarar a ministros o al presidente del Gobierno y ha tenido que reconducir en alguna ocasión una instrucción que ha sido muy cuestionada. A continuación, repasamos cómo ha sido todo el proceso.

Toda la cronología del caso tiene su origen en una denuncia interpuesta por el sindicato ultraderechista de Manos Limpias. Un documento que se basaba en recortes e informaciones publicadas en medios digitales, y de las cuales algunas eran inexactas, como reconoció el propio secretario general de Manos Limpias, que incluso llegó a decir que la denuncia podía contener noticias falsas. Tras ello, se sumaron a la causa la organización ultracatólica Hazte Oír o el partido Iusticia Europa.

Pocos días después llegó uno de los momentos más recordados del caso y de esta legislatura que poco a poco se va acercando a su fin: los cinco días de reflexión de Pedro Sánchez y su carta a la ciudadanía tras conocer la apertura de la investigación a su mujer.

Dos meses después de la apertura de la investigación, Peinado imputó a Begoña Gómez por un presunto delito de corrupción y tráfico de influencias. Bajo sospecha, un software y una cátedra de la Universidad Complutense de Madrid. En julio de ese año, Gómez se acogió a su derecho a no declarar y al poco, Peinado citó como testigo al presidente del Gobierno en la Moncloa . Sánchez despachó rápidamente la citación al acogerse a su derecho a no declarar al ser el marido de la investigada, pero el juez llegó a afirmar que podían sacarse "conclusiones" de su silencio. Horas después de la comparecencia, la Abogacía del Estado, en representación de Presidencia del Gobierno, presentó una querella por prevaricación al no haber permitido a Sánchez declarar por escrito, que se sumaron a las otras dos interpuestas contra el magistrado a lo largo del proceso por su labor durante la instrucción.

Por el camino, el magistrado también había imputado al empresario Juan Carlos Barrabés , adjudicatario de unos contratos sobre los que Peinado ponía el foco. En junio y julio de ese año, la propia UCO descartó en sus informes la apreciación de los delitos que imputaba el juez a la mujer del presidente del Gobierno.

Sin embargo, a la vuelta del parón judicial de verano, Peinado decidió dar un paso más y le imputó dos nuevos delitos: intrusismo y apropiación indebida por el desarrollo del software de la Complutense que dirigía la mujer de Sánchez.

sources.body:
La dona del president espanyol , Begoña Gómez, i la seva assessora seran finalment jutjades per un jurat popular.

El jutge Juan Carlos Peinado ha dictat aquest dilluns l'obertura de judici oral per presumptes delictes de tràfic d'influències i malversació contra Gómez i només malversació per a Cristina Álvarez.

Tal com estava previst, el magistrat les envia a judici abans de jubilar-se aquesta mateixa setmana i rebutja prendre cap mesura cautelar contra elles.

Tanmateix, en la interlocutòria, Peinado sí que ha ordenat investigar "la capacitat econòmica" de Begoña Gómez, a qui ha reclamat que li faci arribar les cinc últimes declaracions de la renda per si cal imposar-li possibles responsabilitats econòmiques.

El magistrat ha acordat per a les dues l'obligació d'estar "en tot moment" a disposició del jutjat i de l'Audiència Provincial de Madrid, òrgan al qual es remetrà la causa perquè dicti data del judici.

Peinado posa fi a una investigació que va arrencar fa gairebé dos anys i mig arran d'una denúncia de Manos Limpias.

El 20 de juny passat, Peinado ja havia decretat l'obertura de judici oral a Begoña Gómez. Llavors portava a judici la dona de Pedro Sánchez per quatre delictes: tràfic d'influències , corrupció en els negocis , malversació de cabals públics i apropiació indeguda .

A més, li va retirar el passaport i li va imposar la prohibició de sortir de territori espanyol.

Però l'Audiència Provincial de Madrid va corregir part de la instrucció del jutge i el va obligar a retirar dos delictes: el de corrupció en els negocis i el d'apropiació indeguda.

A més, el Consell General del Poder Judicial (CGPJ) va obrir un expedient al jutge Peinado per la polèmica interlocutòria en què insinuava que la policia que feia d'escorta a la dona del president espanyol podria ajudar-la a fugir.

Tant Begoña Gómez com Cristina Álvarez demanen la seva absolució , igual que la Fiscalia , que mai no hi ha vist delicte. En canvi, l'acusació popular, liderada per Hazte Oír , demana en total 13 anys de presó per a Gómez i 6 per a la seva assessora.

La Moncloa ha condemnat la decisió del jutge i ha assegurat que, durant la instrucció, ja ha quedat " clara i demostrada la innocència" de Gómez , així com la "intenció política" de la causa.

Mantenim la nostra plena confiança que el jurat serà equànime i impartirà justícia. Es tracta d'una instrucció arbitrària i injusta que només respon a la persecució judicial contra Begoña Gómez.

Denuncien, a més, que s'ha notificat la interlocutòria coincidint amb un viatge del president a l'estranger i han denunciat l'"assetjament i deshumanització" durant tota la instrucció.

Des del PSOE , la secretària d'Organització, Rebeca Torró, en un tuit , ha defensat la innocència de Gómez i ha titllat l'anunci del jutge com l'"últim servei a la pàtria abans de penjar la toga".

No és l'únic maldecap judicial de Sánchez, ja que aquest mateix dilluns hi ha hagut novetats al voltant del cas Plus Ultra.

El jutge de l'Audiència Nacional José Luís Calama ha citat a declarar com a investigades les filles de José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero i li ha donat tres dies perquè entregui "tota la documentació que té al seu poder" sobre les joies que es van trobar a la seva oficina.

stories.headline: Spain says Morocco is cooperating to prevent another mass crossing into Ceuta

sources.body:
Se han cumplido 50 días de la entrada masiva de migrantes a Ceuta y sigue sin haber consenso sobre cuántas personas permanecen en la ciudad autónoma. El número varía en función de la autoridad que lo facilite. El Gobierno ceutí siempre ha dado cifras más altas y el Gobierno central ha corregido al alza las suyas. En VerificaRTVE te contamos los datos más recientes y las discrepancias entre las cifras oficiales que han dado autoridades estatales y locales a lo largo de estas semanas.

El 31 de julio, el Gobierno central cifra en unos 12.500 los migrantes que permanecen en Ceuta. Entonces, el cálculo del Ministerio del Interior y Delegación del Gobierno en Ceuta era que unas 50.000 personas habían participado en la entrada masiva desde Marruecos a Ceuta y, de ellas, más de 37.500 habían retornado.

Desde el Gobierno de Ceuta, su presidente Juan Jesús Vivas cifra en 60.000 las personas que habían entrado , pero no aporta datos de cuántos permanecen en la ciudad autónoma.

Un día después, el 1 de agosto, el ministro del Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, afirma que la cifra de entradas "puede estar entre 50.000 y 60.000 ", y subraya que "es muy difícil" concretar el número de entradas y salidas. Asegura que "casi todos ellos han salido ya de Ceuta".

El 4 de agosto, Interior aumenta a 72.000 los migrantes que entraron a Ceuta y asegura que unos 2.000 permanecen en la ciudad autónoma. Grande-Marlaska anuncia el retorno de 70.000 migrantes de los 72.000 que habrían entrado. El ministro se refiere en rueda de prensa al "retorno de la inmensa mayoría de personas que entraron de forma irregular en España el 30 de julio".

El delegado del Gobierno en Ceuta , Miguel Ángel Pérez, afirma el 5 de agosto en una entrevista con la cadena SER que se están proporcionando "2.000 raciones de comida y bebida a las personas que permanecen en los alrededores del CETI (Centro de Estancia Temporal de Inmigrantes)". Aunque Pérez también señala que en otras zonas del barrio de El Príncipe seguía habiendo personas, por lo que s e estima que el total podría rondar las 2.500.

Sin embargo, las autoridades ceutíes dan la cifra de 5.000 migrantes en Ceuta el 3 de agosto y, cinco días después, elevan el dato hasta los 11.000. El 3 de agosto, en una entrevista con el diario El País , Juan Jesús Vivas, es preguntado por si "todavía hay 5.000 personas en la ciudad ", a lo que contesta: "No tengo datos exactos, pero es lo que percibimos en función de los trabajos que se están haciendo". El 8 de agosto, según el presidente de Ceuta, entre 8.000 y 11.000 los migrantes continúan en Ceuta tras la llegada masiva, como contamos en RTVE Noticias. El presidente ceutí pide al Gobierno más recursos para hacer frente a la situación "insostenible" en la ciudad y el retorno "de todos los que entraron" desde Marruecos. "Miles de personas deambulando por nuestras calles, en nuestras barriadas, en los montes, en las playas...", denuncia Vivas.

A finales de agosto, Interior eleva la cifra de migrantes que siguen en Ceuta a 5.000 y las autoridades ceutíes siguen estimando entre 9.000 y 10.000 personas. El 13 de agosto, Marlaska ya cifra en 5.000 los migrantes que quedan en Ceuta, eleva a 1.898 los menores migrantes identificados y anuncia un refuerzo policial en la frontera.

El govern espanyol treu ferro a les crides que circulen aquests dies animant a una nova entrada massiva a Ceuta aquest dimecres, coincidint amb les eleccions legislatives al Marroc.

El ministre d'Afers Exteriors, José Manuel Albares , ha explicat a "El matí de Catalunya Ràdio" que n'estan al cas, però afegeix que aquestes crides no estan arrelant entre la població marroquina:

No sembla que aquests missatges estiguin calant gaire, però de manera preventiva activem tots els canals que tenim en marxa des del dia 30.

En aquest sentit, Albares ha explicat que està "en contacte permanent" amb les autoritats marroquines perquè a l'altra banda de la frontera "també hi hagi un dispositiu dissuasiu que en cas de necessitat es pugui utilitzar per impedir qualsevol allau".

El ministre ha recordat que el 15 d'agost , quan també van circular crides a una entrada massiva per la frontera de Ceuta, "aquest mecanisme va funcionar perfectament" .

El ministre José Manuel Albares també ha explicat que han activat una campanya a través de xarxes i mitjans de comunicació en què s'avisa els marroquins que entrar de manera irregular a Ceuta i Melilla no dona dret a accedir a la Península, no dona dret a quedar-se a Espanya ni tampoc a moure's lliurement per Europa.

En aquest punt, ha celebrat que la premsa del Marroc "s'està fent ressò de la campanya del ministeri" , tal com ja ho van fer, diu, el 15 d'agost. I ha subratllat la importància de tallar de soca-rel la desinformació per evitar que els joves marroquins arrisquin "el seu futur, els seus diners, inclús les seves vides, posant-se en mans de màfies".

El ministre Albares també ha lamentat l'agressió que va patir aquest diumenge la diputada de l'Assemblea de Ceuta Julia Ferreras . La diputada, del partit d'esquerres autonomista Ceuta Ja!, sortia del port de la ciutat en un cotxe on també viatjava l'activista Rafael Borrego , un dels integrants de la Flotilla a Gaza.

A post shared by Rafa Borrego (@rafaborregop)

Desenes de persones van començar a llançar-los pedres i ous . La Policia Nacional ja va detenir diumenge mateix un jove de 22 anys per haver trencat el vidre del cotxe de la diputada i va identificar una segona persona per resistència a l'autoritat durant els mateixos incidents.

Tot apunta que els haurien pogut confondre amb els integrants de l'organització navarresa Negu Gorriak (Dret a Sostre), que arribaven a la mateixa hora al port de Ceuta per denunciar les suposades agressions de militars contra els migrants.

Els concentrats, que esperaven per protestar contra aquesta entitat, l'acusen de "radical" , "proetarra" i d'anar a Ceuta a "trencar la convivència".

El ministre Albares ha dit que el que va passar al port de Ceuta el "preocupa" perquè "sempre hem admirat" Ceuta i els ceutins per la pluralitat i per la bona convivència entre els veïns independentment de l'origen i les creences religioses.

En aquest punt, ha lligat la crispació que es viu a la ciutat amb els missatges que llança l'extrema dreta a través de les xarxes .

El ministro José Manuel Albares,en una imagen reciente 

El Consejo de Asuntos Generales de la Unión Europea vuelve a debatir hoy la oficialidad del catalán, el gallego y el euskera. El asunto figura en el orden del día de la reunión –Irlanda desempeña la presidencia rotatoria–, pero no se espera que haya ninguna votación.

Ante las reticencias de algunos países europeos –si antes estaban sobre todo en Berlín, ahora es en Roma donde la propuesta no se ve con buenos ojos–, el Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez ha elevado la presión y ha deslizado que no estaría dispuesto a aprobar la adhesión de nuevos estados al club comunitario , con la incorporación de nuevas lenguas, si no se resuelve primero la demanda española.

En la cita de hoy no estará el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores, José Manuel Albares. Al haber solo debate y no votación, irá el Secretario de Estado para la UE, Fernando Sampedro. Ayer, desde la Asamblea General de la ONU en Nueva York, Albares urgió a los socios europeos a alcanzar la unanimidad en este asunto. “España va a dejar muy claro que somos totalmente favorables a la ampliación” de la UE, apuntó en una entrevista. Dijo que “es impensable para España que haya un solo idioma más dentro del régimen lingüístico oficial de la Unión Europea si no lo están también el catalán, el euskera y el gallego”. De todos modos, fuentes consultadas deslizan que “no parece que vaya a cambiar nada” porque, tras la crisis migratoria de Ceuta, la posición del Gobierno en Europa ahora mismo no es la mejor.

Por parte de Junts, Josep Rius subrayó ayer que el Ejecutivo “va tarde” y reclamó “que no centrifugue responsabilidades” en terceros, porque ya se tendría que haber aprobado este asunto.

En JxCat han pasado de valorar los esfuerzos de Albares a criticar que el Gobierno no usara la formación de la Comisión Europea para desbloquear la oficialidad. Evitaron valorar la presión que ejerce ahora la Moncloa a los demás países. En Junts se centran en criticar que no se haya hecho esa presión con los nombramientos del ejecutivo europeo y lamentan que pueda parecer que no se amplía la UE por culpa del catalán.

stories.headline: Spain's Constitutional Court begins deliberations on applying the amnesty law to Catalan independence leaders

sources.body:
Más de dos años después de la aprobación de la ley de amnistía, el Tribunal Constitucional comienza a deliberar este martes sobre el primero de los recursos de los líderes del procés para que se les aplique de manera efectiva esta norma. Concretamente, los magistrados tienen en el orden del día el recurso del exconseller y actual secretario general de Junts, Jordi Turull , para que la ley se pueda aplicar también en referencia a la malversación .

La deliberación sobre todos los recursos que poco a poco abordará el Constitucional llegan después del aval a la medida de gracia por parte del Tribunal de Justicia de la Unión Europea (TJUE) en el mes de julio.

Hasta ahora, el Supremo ha descartado aplicar la amnistía al delito de malversación. El alto tribunal entiende que ese delito, que habrían cometido los políticos independentistas procesados, entraría en las excepciones de la ley de amnistía porque, aunque no obtuvieron ningún tipo de ingresos si hubo enriquecimiento indirecto al destinar recursos públicos al referéndum del 1 de octubre de 2017.

Ya se conoció hace unos días que el magistrado conservador del Tribunal Constitucional, José María Macías , apoyaba el rechazo del Tribunal Supremo a aplicar la amnistía a los líderes del procés al apreciar malversación de caudales públicos, según el borrador de su ponencia sobre el recurso de amparo del exconsejero catalán Jordi Turull.

En ese borrador, al que tuvo acceso RTVE, el magistrado señalaba que "la interpretación llevada a cabo por la Sala Segunda del Tribunal Supremo no puede tildarse de sorpresiva o imprevisible, y mucho menos de caprichosa o fruto de una supuesta animadversión hacia el recurrente, sino que se ajusta a la doctrina vigente sobre los elementos del tipo penal de la malversación ".

Asimismo, considera que frente a la tesis de que solo hay enriquecimiento si aumenta el activo de una persona, el borrador avala el criterio del Tribunal Supremo según el cual evitar un desembolso propio o disponer de dinero ajeno constituye un beneficio patrimonial .

Sin embargo, todo apunta a que la mayoría progresista del Constitucional rechazará esta ponencia y que se designará a otro magistrado para que elabore una nueva. En este caso, la resolución definitiva sobre el recurso de Jordi Turull se podría conocer en el próximo pleno , que está fijado para el 6 de octubre.

La sesión de este martes en el Tribunal Constitucional arranca a las 10.30 horas y el recurso de Turull se podría abordar este mismo martes , aunque el pleno se alargará hasta el jueves. La resolución que tomen los magistrados marcará la pauta para el resto de casos ; esto quiere decir que el regreso del expresident Carles Puigdemont a España podría estar cada vez más cerca.

Concretamente, la sentencia del TC precipitaría el futuro del expresident de la Generalitat (sobre el que pesa una orden nacional de detención), en tanto el magistrado del Supremo Pablo Llarena prevé aplicar la doctrina que fije la corte de garantías sin esperar a que esta resuelva su recurso.

Autobuses circulando por la avenida Diagonal en Barcelona. / Zowy Voeten

Las líneas de autobús de Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) se verán afectdas por una huelga parcial que dejará servicios mínimos entre las 10 y las 17 horas de este martes. La convocatoria llega después de meses de negociación del nuevo convenio colectivo y de 23 reuniones sin acuerdo, según han explicado el comité de empresa.

La afectación alcanza todas las líneas operadas por la red de autobuses de TMB , en la que se prevén frecuencias de paso mucho más bajas y tiempos de espera superiores a los habituales. Entre los servicios afectados se encuentran:

El Nitbus no forma parte de la red de autobuses de TMB afectada por esta convocatoria ya que el paro corresponde a los trabajadores del servicio de bus de TMB y está programado en horario diurno. Además, la convocatoria de TMB no incluye a las líneas metropolitanas explotadas por otros operadores de autobús.

La huelga empezará a las 10 de la mañana y finalizará a las 17 de la tarde . Durante las primeras seis horas del paro, hasta las 16, circulará aproximadamente uno de cada cinco autobuses previstos, de acuerdo con los servicios mínimos anunciados. En la última hora, el porcentaje aumentará hasta el 40%.

El Metro de Barcelona no está incluido en estos paros y mantiene su servicio, por lo que será una de las principales alternativas para moverse por la ciudad durante las siete horas de huelga. Tampoco forman parte de este conflicto laboral los servicios de Tram, Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat de Catalunya (FGC) y Rodalies, por lo que pueden servir como alternativas en aquellos trayectos donde exista conexión .

La recomendación para quienes tengan que desplazarse entre las 10:00 y las 17:00 horas es planificar el recorrido con antelación y priorizar, siempre que sea posible, Metro, tren o tranvía para evitar las mayores esperas previstas en las paradas de autobús.

La protesta se produce en el contexto de las negociaciones para renovar el convenio colectivo de la plantilla de autobuses . Los representantes de los trabajadores han convocado el paro después de 23 reuniones de negociación sin que se haya alcanzado un acuerdo. La huelga cuenta con el respaldo de los sindicatos ACAT, ACTUB, CCOO, CGT, SIT y UGT .

Els treballadors del bus de Barcelona faran una aturada de set hores aquest dimarts, entre les 10.00 i les 17.00, per celebrar una assemblea extraordinària a les Cotxeres de Sants, on decidirà si inicia un període de mobilitzacions.

S'han fixat uns serveis mínims del 20% entre les 10h i les 16h. Entre les 16h i les 17h, quan la vaga coincideix amb l'hora punta, el servei mínim serà del 40% . També s'haurà de garantir un bus de barri per línia i el personal indispensable per mantenir les infraestructures necessàries per al funcionament dels serveis mínims i el reinici de la circulació.

La plantilla denuncia el bloqueig en la negociació per les condicions laborals del nou conveni en aspectes com l'augment salarial o la reducció de la jornada. Els representants de la plantilla diuen estar en un "punt crític" davant la "pèrdua continuada de poder adquisitiu dels empleats".

Han optat per una aturada temporal com a "mesura de força" per garantir el dret de la plantilla a assistir a una assemblea general extraordinària a les Cotxeres de Sants .

Després de 23 reunions de conveni "sense avenços significatius", doncs, el comitè d'empresa ha decidit convocar l'assemblea perquè siguin els empleats els que decideixin els pròxims passos.

El comitè d'empresa considera que "la direcció no té intenció d'arribar a cap mena d'acord". Així, critiquen falta d'entesa en temes com l' augment salarial , la reducció de la jornada a 35 hores setmanals, la millora de calendaris per a tots els col·lectius o el lot de Nadal .

D'altra banda, el comitè d'empresa assegura que "es continuen sense aplicar els descansos mínims legals al personal de conducció". Un dret que recorden que és "elemental, indiscutible i innegociable" i no "una moneda de canvi en una mesa de conveni".

Un dels pocs àmbits on sí que hi ha acords és en la millora de permisos i llicències , on els treballadors dels busos de Barcelona equipararien els seus drets d'absència laboral als dels empleats del metro.
sources.headline: Aturada als busos de Barcelona entre les 10 i les 17 h d'avui per debatre noves mobilitzacions

sources.body:
Toc d’inici a la vaga de set hores dels conductors d’autobús de Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) . Aquest dimarts a les deu han començat les aturades al servei, que s’allargaran fins a les cinc de la tarda amb l’objectiu de facilitar que la plantilla pugui assistir a l’ assemblea general de treballadors que tindrà lloc a dos quarts d’una a les cotxeres de Sants . La mobilització dels conductors es produeix després que en el darrer any no s’hagi pogut negociar un nou conveni col·lectiu per a aquesta part de la plantilla de TMB.

“Aquest comitè d’empresa, fart de l’actitud de la direcció de l’empresa, va votar en l’últim ple aquesta convocatòria de vaga. Des del novembre del 2025 s’està negociant el conveni que ens ha de regir en els pròxims anys. Després de 23 reunions infructuoses sense, pràcticament, cap acord, la paciència ha arribat a un límit . És hora d’explicar a la plantilla la situació actual i que decideixi, com a col·lectiu, la resposta a aquesta situació”, assenyalaven els representants dels treballadors en un contundent comunicat fet públic la setmana passada. Els intents a última hora de la comanyia per evitar la vaga han resultat infructuosos i, després de quatre reunions de mediació, el comitè d’empresa decidia aquest dilluns al vespre de forma unànime mantenir l’aturada parcial per fer l’assemblea amb la plantilla.

Cal recordar que les reivindicacions parteixen de la necessitat de conciliar la vida laboral i familiar treballant menys temps. Per fer-ho, demanen més contractació per poder repartir les tasques entre més personal. “L’aplicació de les 35 hores i uns descansos, coherents amb el segle en què vivim, permetrà un millor servei que repercutirà en la seguretat de la societat barcelonina, amb personal de conducció descansat i sense una afectació greu de l’estrès inherent a la difícil circulació d’aquesta ciutat”, apunten els treballadors. I afegeixen: “Les mobilitzacions són per necessitat, ja que la càrrega de treball cada vegada és major en tots els col·lectius. No entenem que una empresa pública es gestioni per rendiments econòmics, i no per garantir el servei públic de transport”.

Els conductors de bus no són els únic membres de la plantilla de TMB en peu de guerra. Els empleats del telefèric de Montjuïc també han convocat tres dies de vaga coincidint amb les festes de la Mercè també amb l’objectiu d’aconseguir “ millores socials i unes condicions laborals més dignes “. En un comunicat, la plataforma Som Telefèric En Lluita explica que la mobilització impulsada pel sindicat Solidaritat Obrera tindrà lloc tant el 24 i 26 de setembre com l’11 d’octubre, amb aturades que seran de dues hores i afectaran una franja del migdia, de dos quarts d’una a dos quarts de tres, i una altra de la tarda, de tres quarts de quatre a tres quarts de sis. Els empleats lamenten les possibles molèsties que puguin causar amb aquestes mesures, però asseguren que el seu posicionament és una resposta a l’actitud “ immobilista ” per part de TMB a l’hora d’abordar una sèrie de millores plantejades pels treballadors.
